title: HB1306 (2026 Regular): Assisted Outpatient Treatment - Surrender or Seizure of Firearms

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2026RS/bills/hb/hb1306f.pdf)
provenance.note: First reader (as filed); no passage vote recorded. Effective October 1, 2026, and abrogated if the Chapter 704 (2024) termination provision takes effect.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Health – General § 10–6A–08.1(B)): (B) (1) IF A COURT ORDERS A RESPONDENT TO COMPLY WITH ASSISTED OUTPATIENT TREATMENT UNDER § 10–6A–08 OF THIS SUBTITLE, THE COURT SHALL MAKE A DETERMINATION AS TO WHETHER THE RESPONDENT IS LIKELY TO ENDANGER OR CAUSE PHYSICAL INJURY TO THE RESPONDENT OR ANOTHER IF THE RESPONDENT HAS ACCESS TO A FIREARM. (2) IF THE COURT DETERMINES THAT THE RESPONDENT IS LIKELY TO ENDANGER OR CAUSE PHYSICAL INJURY TO THE RESPONDENT OR ANOTHER IF THE RESPONDENT HAS ACCESS TO A FIREARM, THE COURT SHALL ORDER THE RESPONDENT: (I) TO SURRENDER TO LAW ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITIES ANY FIREARM IN THE RESPONDENT’S POSSESSION; AND (II) NOT TO PURCHASE OR POSSESS ANY FIREARM FOR THE DURATION OF THE ORDER REQUIRING THE RESPONDENT TO COMPLY WITH ASSISTED OUTPATIENT TREATMENT.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Health – General § 10–6A–08.1(C)(1)): (1) IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROVISIONS OF § 1–203 OF THE CRIMINAL PROCEDURE ARTICLE, ON APPLICATION BY A STATE’S ATTORNEY OR A LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER WITH PROBABLE CAUSE TO BELIEVE THAT A RESPONDENT WHO IS SUBJECT TO AN ORDER UNDER THIS SECTION POSSESSES A FIREARM AND FAILED TO SURRENDER THE FIREARM, A COURT MAY ISSUE A SEARCH WARRANT FOR THE REMOVAL OF THE FIREARM AT ANY LOCATION IDENTIFIED IN THE APPLICATION FOR THE WARRANT.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Health – General § 10–6A–08.1(H)(4)(III)): (III) SUBJECT TO SUBPARAGRAPH (II) OF THIS PARAGRAPH, ON REQUEST OF THE RESPONDENT, A LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY SHALL RETURN ALL FIREARMS BELONGING TO THE RESPONDENT NOT LATER THAN 48 HOURS AFTER THE EXPIRATION OF AN ORDER UNDER THIS SECTION.
